comparison: RDKit RunReactants on the reactant (AddHs for hydrogens=explicit_h), each product set sanitized (SanitizeMol, RemoveHs) and written as canonical SMILES; unsanitizable sets dropped.

probes.note: `[ca]` is aromatic carbon AND aromatic (not calcium); likewise `[na]`, `[cr6]`. chematic <= 1.0.38 read Ca/Na/Cr and matched nothing.
`[cr6]` is aromatic carbon in a 6-ring, not chromium.
An element change takes the template atom's charge (0), not the matched atom's: CS(C)(C)C.
H count re-derived for the new element: CS.
The rewritten ring atom keeps the reactant's aromatic flag; sanitize kekulizes it as hypervalent S: ClS1=CC=CC=N1.
With AddHs the H atom stays on the new S and RDKit gives [SH2]; the implicit-H form gives the H-free thioether.
The raw product is one graph; RDKit's kekulization of the ring cation depends on atom order ([c+]1ccccc1C vs Cc1[c+]cccc1 give different Kekule structures).
